recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No follow-up is needed for FHIR-6950 unless Patient Care later revisits Communication receipt semantics.
issue_request: Published Patient Care change request for DSTU1 Communication.recipient 0..* asking how a sender can know whether a multi-recipient message was received by all recipients. The accepted Persuasive with Modification resolution required a usage note that individual receipt tracking needs a separate Communication resource instance per recipient, while multi-recipient communications are for untracked or aggregate receipt scenarios.
initial_application: No Jira-keyed FHIR-6950 commit was found. The resolved note was present in the old Communication spreadsheet by commit 8af82e04026d1c904036e5c48529d6d93387c295, which QA-cleaned the wording, and it was carried into the current StructureDefinition source by the 2021 source rework commit 33b409a4b6d544598262f2f074ebb4b6dc466157.
additional_context: Communication is active in source/fhir.ini under [resources], assigned to Patient Care, and approved. Current source includes Communication.sent, Communication.received, and Communication.recipient; recipient carries the individual-vs-aggregate receipt note. Jira searches found no later FHIR-core issue changing this rule, and Zulip/Confluence searches found no relevant FHIR-6950 discussion or references.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current build-scoped StructureDefinition already conveys the resolved rule with equivalent wording, and adding parallel narrative text would be redundant rather than a necessary specification correction.
